bugClass.title: Ignored items never return to their prior status
bugClass.cause: Persisting an ignored-until timestamp and prior status without a hub-owned lifecycle sweep that detects expiry and restores the item leaves it ignored indefinitely. The same omission can affect other persisted pause, park, reminder, or scheduled-run transitions when their due time passes without a corresponding restoration or transition.
bugClass.criteria: A site exhibits this cause if it persists an ignored/parked state and expiry time (optionally with the prior state) but has no hub-owned runtime process that finds expired records and restores their prior status; or if an equivalent persisted pause/reminder/scheduled transition has no due-time processor to apply the required transition. Require evidence of both persisted state and the missing or ineffective expiry-driven transition; generic timers or deadlines alone do not qualify.

candidates.evidence: `src/utils/projects-sessions/trackerItemTransitions.ts:160-161` persists `ignored_until` from `body.until` and saves the prior status in `ignored_prev_status` when setting status to `ignored`. The excerpt does not establish whether a hub-owned sweep later finds expired items and restores that status.

The repository selects rows with `status = 'ignored'` and non-null `ignored_until`, then calls `plan(row)` and commits rows the plan selects (lines 6–17). This shows a possible restoration mechanism, but the excerpt does not show when `restore` is called, whether a hub-owned process invokes it after expiry, or what the plan checks. Evidence is incomplete for establishing either the required expiry sweep or its absence.

`src/adapters/projects-sessions/TrackerSchemaAdapter.ts:63-64` includes `ignored_until` and `ignored_prev_status` in the adapter's field list, but the excerpt only shows schema field names; it does not establish an expiry-triggered restoration path or its absence.

`src/utils/projects-sessions/planTrackerItemMutation.types.ts:15-17` declares snapshot fields including `remind_at` and `ignored_prev_status`. This type declaration establishes neither that these states are persisted here nor whether any due-time processor applies the required transition.

This test shows ignore persists `ignored_until` and `ignored_prev_status`, and that an explicit `unignore` restores the prior status (lines 154–162). It does not establish whether a hub-owned expiry processor runs; a test excerpt alone cannot show that the processor is missing.

The normalizer maps `parked_until` and `ignored_until` to date/instant normalizers (lines 75–77). It shows field normalization only; it does not establish a persisted status transition or the presence or absence of a hub-owned expiry-driven restore.
